text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 3.2% today, breaking a two-week downtrend that has wiped out 9% of the stock's value since late October. The immediate trigger appears to be uncertainty around the company's recent leadership change and corporate update announced on October 29th—details that would directly affect investor confidence in refiner profitability and strategy—combined with a broader market caution warned by analysts ahead of Big Oil earnings reports, where forward guidance could disappoint.

The stock's weakness also reflects mixed signals in refining economics: while crude oil prices have climbed today following U.S. military strikes on Iran, U.S. refineries are running at 92.8% capacity with elevated fuel inventories (209 million barrels of gasoline, 103 million of diesel). High capacity utilization and full storage tanks limit a refiner's ability to profit from rising oil prices, since they can't easily ramp up production or command premium pricing when the market is already saturated with fuel.
